row.evidence: Certinia (formerly FinancialForce) is built on Salesforce: its apps are licensed managed packages whose licences are assigned to Salesforce users in Setup, and Certinia says user management and access control come from the Salesforce platform; Certinia documents no SCIM endpoint of its own.
row.notes: New row. Quote-only: certinia.com/pricing redirects to Request a demo, no public plans. Certinia's PSA, ERP and Customer Success clouds run as Salesforce managed packages: users are Salesforce users in the customer's org, given Certinia package licences and permission sets in Salesforce Setup. No Certinia SCIM endpoint, IdP app or user API exists, so status is none (by absence, help-centre sitemap of 8,451 topics has no SCIM/SSO/provisioning topic). In practice user lifecycle follows the customer's Salesforce provisioning (Salesforce's own SSO/SCIM, not researched here because it is not Certinia's domain); assigning Certinia package licences is a separate Setup step. Flag for merge: arguably 'inherits Salesforce' rather than 'No SCIM'.

scim.notes: No Certinia SCIM endpoint. Identity, SSO and user lifecycle are those of the underlying Salesforce org; Certinia access is a managed-package licence plus permission sets.

limitations.text: Package licences for Certinia apps are assigned per Salesforce user in Setup > Installed Packages > Manage Licenses.

user_api.notes: Certinia publishes Apex/product APIs for its own objects (Technical Pack); no Certinia user-management API. Users and licence assignment are managed with Salesforce Setup and Salesforce APIs.

okta.notes: No Certinia or FinancialForce OIN app; customers sign in through Salesforce.

fallbacks.other_sync: Users are Salesforce users in the customer's org; Certinia package licences and permission sets are assigned in Salesforce Setup, so provisioning follows the customer's Salesforce user provisioning
